fields.paraphrase: Pleased by humility, Kumāras say they desire no task and are naked, have come because they heard king’s fame in heaven, and ask permission to return Brahmaloka. Pṛthu says he has enjoyed kingdom/varied pleasures and now asks yoga for peace. Recognizing qualification/disenchantment, they teach that full Gaṇeśa yoga-peace is to be worshipped with great devotion for peace. This is teacher exchange, not a direct new Gaṇeśa appearance.

fields.paraphrase: Kumāras fall silent/prostrate; devotion-bound child Vināyaka says hymn gives yoga-peace to readers/hearers and he will give the desired object while himself moved by the hymn; Kumāras will become Gaṇapatyas like Śiva. No request words or Pṛthu-directed boon here. Child then plays with children like ordinary child. Kumāras visit Kāśī king, are honored, eat and return to their place. They conclude Pṛthu should worship Gaṇeśa as full peace-knowledge.

reason: Independent whole2.25 review: first-person dāsyāmi stotrabhāvitaḥ describes Vināyaka as hymn-moved giver, not a reader eligibility condition.
